title: First halting time
statement: Let $M$ be a machine on Boolean inputs, let $c_0$ be a configuration, and let $T$ be a natural number. If the run from $c_0$ is halted at time $T$, then there is a time $t\le T$ such that it is not halted at any earlier time and its configuration at time $t$ equals its configuration at time $T$.
hypotheses_covered: The run from $c_0$ is halted at time $T$
replaced:
If a machine's run from $c_0$ is halted at time $T$, then there is a time
$t \le T$ at which it halts for the first time: the machine is live at every time
before $t$, and its configuration at time $t$ equals its configuration at time
$T$.
